items.review_rationale: Read the full metric axioms for a nonempty set and real-valued distance: diagonal zero, positive separation off diagonal, symmetry and triangle inequality.

references.context: The metric-space formulation explicitly rules out the empty set.
d(x,x)=0 for all x and d(x,y)>0 for distinct x,y, giving nonnegativity.
Interchanging ordered inputs does not change the metric value.
Distance comparison for every triple of elements of X.

references.disposition: The axioms impose distances abstractly, not a particular coordinate norm.

items.review_rationale: Read the topology generated by metric balls, comparison of (X,d) to its canonical triple and the condition tau=tau_d, preserving distinction between compatible metric and metrizable topology.

references.context: Set of y∈X with d(x,y)<r for a positive real radius r.
Topology generated by all metric open balls as a basis.
Topological and metric structures over the same set, with topology exactly that induced by d.

references.phrase: metrizable topology may admit multiple metrics
references.disposition: Existence of a compatible metric alone does not identify which metric is specified.

items.review_rationale: Read a norm on a vector space over a normed division ring with the scalar modulus supplied by K; retained norm values in nonnegative reals, positive definiteness, absolute homogeneity and triangle inequality.

references.context: Specified map assigning a nonnegative real magnitude to each vector.
Zero norm occurs if and only if the vector equals the zero vector.
For every scalar a and vector v, ∥av∥=|a|_K∥v∥.
For any v,w, norm of v+w is no greater than sum of norms.

references.disposition: Homogeneity is stated as ∥av∥ using a left vector space; right-module variants require their own compatible action.

items.review_rationale: Read norm on real or complex vector space with real-valued nonnegative output, positive definiteness, scalar modulus homogeneity and triangle inequality, distinct from division-ring generality.

references.phrase: vector space V over R or C
real absolute value for real scalars

references.context: Usual modulus |a| of a complex number used in the norm homogeneity axiom.
Vector magnitude function into nonnegative real numbers.
Only the zero vector has zero norm.
For all real or complex scalars a, ∥av∥=|a|∥v∥.

references.disposition: The source is specialized to conventional R or C scalars rather than arbitrary normed division rings.
